title: Benchmark coverage: which rule shapes the final run really tests
subtitle: The 8 Declare templates, hard or soft, with or without a goal: 32 cells. The card fixes raised the well-tested cells from 15 to 18. A soft rule beside a goal is still never judged.

blocks.title: In plain words
blocks.text: The final run trains on benchmark cards. A card holds a task in plain words, the clauses a correct Reward Machine needs, the level it runs on, and scripted plans that must pass or break those clauses. The rule shapes are the 8 Declare templates the generator may write, each hard or soft, with or without a goal: 32 cells. A cell is tested well when a trained card on a level that forces the choice judges that rule. Two reviews on 2026-11-20, before and after the card fixes, read every card against that bar. The fixes took the well-tested cells from 15 to 18 of 32. The biggest hole stays: a soft rule beside a hard goal is never judged.

items: **Two reviews, one bar.** The baseline review (main `d4e09fe`) read all 111 cards, reran all 660 scripted plans and swept all 165 accepted answers. The delta review read the card fixes before they merged. Both used Opus 5.5, no model call and no training.

**The fixes reached main** in `ab27c07` (merged as `b3ba9ef`): stated orders required, answers that skip a stated clause removed, 3 seeds, 7 idle-passable, weak or unsolved-level cards stopped, and `tpl-responded-existence-2-nogoal` plus 2 new service-room cards started. A second round on the same branch fixed two of the delta review's findings and added `tpl-existence-two-5-nogoal`.
**Every sample below carries its task, clauses, LTLf and Reward Machine**, compiled from the pinned cards of main `6606ab7` with the repository's compiler (`check/card_machines.py`).

**Counting caveat.** The baseline review wrote 15 well-tested cells beside 8 not judged, 4 gaps and 2 weak, which leaves 3 cells unnamed. Read with the delta review's labels, its table gives 16, so the fixes added the 2 RespondedExistence cells.

items: **Pay-order flag, class A.** The pay order check wants a started task to pay more than one never started. These machines pay both 0; the user ruled them fine and postponed the check change, but the pre-training gate still blocks them. The 7 trained: `cx-siren`, `tpl-absence-1-goal` (one other answer), `tpl-not-co-existence-1-goal`, `tpl-responded-existence-4-goal` and the soft goal cards for Precedence, RespondedExistence and NotCoExistence.

**Card issue** covers idle-passable cards, an unsolved level, answers that drop a stated rule, a missing "then", stale notes and settings the shop has not been tested with. The per-card list is in `evidence/card-review-report.md`.

items.title: A soft rule beside a goal is never judged
items.text: On the 8 soft goal template cards and `cx-goal-one-rule`, `cx-goal-many-rules`, an agent passes by reaching the goal. How often it breaks the soft rule is reported, but no bar says how often is too often.
items.inset: Waits on a user decision, for example: goal reached and fewer soft breaks than the breaking plan or the run without a Reward Machine.

items.title: Two hard rules have no card without a goal
items.text: Hard Precedence and hard NotCoExistence train only beside a goal. No trained card checks them alone.
items.inset: Hard copies of the soft Lanes cards would close both. User decision.

items.title: Some hard cards pass for free
items.text: On `tpl-existence-1-goal` the level forces the pickup, so any agent that reaches the goal passes. On the two ExistenceTwo cards the count comes free: the box falls 2 to 6 steps after a pickup, and a key not dropped at once is already held on two moves.
items.inset: `tpl-existence-two-5-nogoal` (kill two zombies) is the event-based count the delta review asked for; it came after the count and is not judged yet.

items.title: Soft Absence counts one break per episode
items.text: On Lanes, letting one zombie through and letting ten through both count as one break, so halving the breaches shows no gain.
items.inset: Count break steps for Absence. Test design.

items.title: The siren-room "if" rule acts as a plain must
items.text: The siren always rings by step 4 and the switch is out of reach before then, so "if the siren rings, flip the switch" behaves as "flip the switch". The cards test the obligation and the template the generator writes, not the condition.
items.inset: Delta review P3; no change made.

items.title: Two base cards still score the goal alone as right
items.text: `base-unlock-pickup` and `base-key-corridor` keep both orders optional (`forced`). `Existence(box)` alone scores exact, while one `Existence` per stated step, what the generator rules ask for a list, scores as a mismatch.
items.inset: Delta review finding 1, P1. The user picks the reading (the list states an order or not). Still open on main `6606ab7`.

items: **Not a matrix cell, still blocking the freeze.** KeyCorridorS6R3 learned in 0 of 71 runs and still holds `base-key-corridor` and `cx-sequence`; the shop learned only with promise cost or end judgment on, and its final settings (embeddings, default promise cost) are untested; 18 trained template cards and the `lanes-rules` ablation have no bundles yet.

**Fixed in the second round.** The two `NotCoExistence` answers that accept the same runs as the removed `Absence` (`tpl-precedence-2/3-goal`) are gone, and `cx-sequence` paraphrase 3 now reads "and then pick up the ball".
**What these cards check.** Judged success: every hard clause holds (goal reached in the stated order).
**Family.** Precedence chain + Existence(goal) (form B), hard, on MiniGrid DoorKey, UnlockPickup, BlockedUnlockPickup, KeyCorridorS6R3.
**Cards (5).** `base-doorkey`, `base-unlock-pickup`, `base-blocked-unlock-pickup`, `base-key-corridor`, `cx-sequence`.

items: **Review note.** Each is covered by a trained forcing card: lanes-rules, lanes-guard, keygift-hard and the forced Response copy, tpl-responded-existence-2-nogoal, tpl-existence-two-4-goal, tpl-responded-existence-4-goal.
**Review note.** The 'Then' after an 'if' rule question now touches only generation cards (tpl-response-2/3-goal, tpl-responded-existence-1/2/3-goal); no trained card depends on it.

**Reviews.** `evidence/card-review-report.md` (baseline: verdicts, ranked fixes, matrix, per-card issues) and `evidence/delta-review.md` (the delta pass: findings, checks, the after matrix). Both are the reviewers' text returns, copied by the coordinator.
**Groups.** `evidence/groups.json` (baseline, 9 groups on 53 cards) and `evidence/groups-v2.json` (after the fixes, 10 groups with the samples and notes shown here).

**Card fixes.** `evidence/card-fix-report.json` (round 1: every changed field with its rule, the sweep counts, the two new cards, record mismatches, what was left undone) and `evidence/card-fix-round2.out` (round 2: answers removed and added).
**Checks.** `evidence/delta-checks/`: the trace-bank summaries of every suite (`tb-*.out`) and the answer sweep (`sweep.out`) the delta review ran.
**Cards.** `evidence/cards/<suite>/tasks.json`: the cards of main `6606ab7`, which the samples are compiled from.
**Graphs.** `graphs/<card>.rm`, `.svg` and `.html` for 24 sample cards (`render-rm --html`). `shop-boil` is too large to draw (65 states, 10,662 transitions) and has no file.

**Not copied.** The sweep and trace-bank scripts the reviews used and their raw outputs (`sweep.jsonl`, 20 MB of traces). They stay in `.git/agent-memory/plans/farm-final-20261119/` (`card-review/`, `card-fix/`): review prototypes, not kept to the repository's lint rules.
